State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Divisional Manager, National ... vs U. Balu, S/O. Uttrapathy, Illayakudi ... on 11 September, 2013
IN THE TAMIL NADU STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL
 COMMISSION, MADURAI BENCH.

Present: Thiru.J.JAYARAM, M.A. M.L., Presiding Judicial Member
 Thiru.S. SAMBANDAM, B.Sc., Member

 F.A.No.284/2012
 (F.A.No.996/2011 on the file of State Consumer Disputes Redressal
 Commission, Chennai.)

 (Against the order in C.C.No.106/2007, dated 25.08.2010 on the file of DCDRF,
 Thanjavur)

 WEDNESDAY, THE 11th DAY OF SEPTEMBER 2013.

Divisional Manager,
National Insurance Co., Ltd.,
62, T.S.R. Big Street,
Kumbakonam. Appellant/1st opposite Party

 Vs

1. U. Balu,
 S/o. Uttrapathy,
 Illayakudi Village, Alaveli Post,
 Seerkazhi Taluk,
 Nagapattinam District. 1st Respondent/Complainant

2. Raman & Raman Motors,
 48, Thiruvidaimaruthur Road,
 Kumbakonam. 2nd Respondent/2nd opposite Party

3. HDFC Bank Ltd.,
 A-10, Lakshmi Arcade,
 11th Cross, Thillai Nagar,
 Thiruchirappalli - 620 018. 3rd Respondent/3rd Opposite party
 2

For Appellants/1st opposite party: Mr.K. Chandrasekaran, Advocate.

For Respondents 1 to 3/Complainant, Ops 2 & 3: Served. Called absent.

 This appeal coming before us for final hearing on 07.08.2013 and on

hearing the arguments of appellant side and upon perusing the material records

this Commission made the following:

 ORDER
Thiru. J. JAYARAM, PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER.
1. The appeal is filed by the 1st opposite party against the order of the

District Forum, Thanjavur in C.C.No.106/2007, dated 25.08.2010, allowing the

complaint against the 1st opposite party.
2. The case of the complainant is that he purchased a motor cycle from

the 2nd opposite party availing loan from the 3rd opposite party and his vehicle

was insured with the 1st opposite party. The vehicle was stolen away on

21.01.2007 and the loss of motorcycle was intimated to the police; but the

vehicle could not be traced. He submitted claim form to the insurer/1st opposite

party but the claim was repudiated by the 1st opposite party without any valid

reason, which amounts to deficiency in service on the part of the 1 st opposite

party and hence the complainant praying for direction to the opposite parties to

pay jointly and severally a sum of Rs.43,224/- which is the amount paid to the

2nd opposite party and to pay compensation.
3. According to the 1st opposite party, the complainant's vehicle was not

registered with the Registering Authority/Regional Transport Office and further
3
the loss of motorcycle was reported only on 29.03.2007 to the 1st opposite party

and to the Police belatedly and hence the complainant is not entitled to claim

compensation under the policy and the claim was repudiated for valid reasons

and there is no deficiency in service on their part.
4. The District Forum considered the rival contentions and allowed the

complaint holding that there is deficiency in service on the part of the 1st

opposite party and passed an order directing the 1st opposite party to pay

Rs.40,775/- which is the cost of the motorcycle and to pay costs of Rs.1000/-.

Aggrieved by the impugned order the 1st opposite party/National Insurance

Company has preferred this appeal.
5. The contention of the appellant/1st opposite party would be that the

complainant's vehicle was insured with them and the vehicle was lost on

21.01.2007 and the vehicle was not registered with the Registering

Authority/Regional Transport Officer at the time of theft and the vehicle was

used by the complainant without registration in violation of the provisions of
Motor Vehicles Act
and the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and

hence the claim was repudiated and there is no deficiency in service on their

part.
6. On perusal of Ex A3, the Policy was in force from 01.12.2006 to

30.11.2007 and the vehicle was purchased on 30.11.2006 and theft of the

vehicle took pace on 21.01.2007 and therefore the policy was very much in force

on the date of theft. However, admittedly, the vehicle was purchased on
4
30.11.2006 and the vehicle was lost on 21.01.2007 and theft has been reported

to the police only on 13.02.2007 after 23 days after the incident as seen from

FIR, Ex A7 and intimation has been sent to insurer/1st opposite party only on

09.03.2007, after a delay of 47 days. Therefore, it is clear that the complainant

has been using the vehicle from 30.11.2006 to 21.01.2007 without registration

with the Registering Authority.
7. In these circumstances, the appellant has argued that the

respondent/complainant is not entitled to compensation under the policy and the

appellant relied on the decisions of the Hon'ble National Consumer Disputes

Redressal Commission reported in I (2013) CPJ 32B (NC) (CN) in the case

Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., - Vs - K.M. Thirunavukkarasu wherein

it has been held as follows: "
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
-
Sections 2(1)(g)
,
21(b)
-
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
-
Sections 39
,
41
, 44 - Insurance - Accidents

claim - Invalidity of registration number - Violation of conditions of policy -

Claim repudiated - Alleged deficiency in service - District Forum allowed

complaint - State Commission dismissed appeal - Hence, revision - Complainant

failed to obtain permanent registration number for the vehicle before expiry of

temporary registration number or even several days thereafter - He had taken

calculated risk in not registering vehicle with concerned registering authority -

Complainant cannot seek any benefit under
section 44
of Motor Vehicles Act,

1988 - Repudiation justified.
5
8. The appellant further relied on the decision of Hon'ble National

Commission, reported in II (2013) CPJ 20A (NC) (CN) in the case of
Narinder Singh - Vs New India Assurance Co., Ltd., & Ors
wherein it has

been held as follows: "
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
-
Sections 2(1)(g)
,
21(b)
-
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
-
Sections 39
, 192 - Insurance - Accident of

vehicle - Surveyor appointed - Loss assessed - Invalid Registration - Claim

repudiated - Alleged deficiency in service - District Forum allowed complaint -

State Commission allowed appeal - Hence revision - Vehicle was being driven

without registration at the time of accident which is prohibited under
section 39
of Act, 1988 - This is also an offence under
Section 192
of Act, 1988 - State

Commission rightly dismissed complaint.
9. The appellant also relied on the decision of the Hon'ble National

Commission reported in IV (2012) CPJ 570 (NC) in the case of
Attar Singh

& Anr - Vs - Reliance General Insurance Co., & Anr
wherein it has been

held as follows: "
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
-
Sections 2(1)(g)
,
14(1)(d)
,
21(b)
- Insurance - Theft of vehicle - Delay in lodging FIR and sending

information to Insurance Company - Claim repudiated - Alleged deficiency in

service - District Forum allowed complaint - State Commission allowed appeal -

Hence revision - FIR was lodged after a delay of 27 days from commission of

theft - Information was sent to Insurance Company about theft with delay of

283 days - Terms and conditions of insurance policy stipulate that petitioners
6
were required to intimate Insurance, Company immediately about theft -

Repudiation justified."
10. In the light of the above decisions of Hon'ble National Commission,

we hold that the respondent/complainant is not entitled to claim the benefits

under the policy and that there is no deficiency in service on the part of the 1 st

opposite party in repudiating the claim of the complainant.
11. The District Forum has erroneously held that there is deficiency in

service on the part of the 1st opposite party and has allowed the complaint

granting compensation. In view of our finding that there is no deficiency on the

part of the 1st opposite party, the order of the District Forum is liable to be set

aside.
12. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the order of the District

Forum is set aside and the complaint is dismissed. No order as to costs in this

appeal.
13. The Registry is directed to hand over the Fixed Deposit Receipt

made towards the mandatory deposit to the appellant/1st opposite party duly

discharged with accrued interest.
Sd/-S. SAMBANDAM, Sd/-J. JAYARAM,
 MEMBER. PRESIDNG JUDICIAL MEMBER.
